The test image shows a green stem segment with dense white cottony/fluffy mycelial growth spreading from it onto a surface. This is clearly a stem disease.

From the part index, stem candidates include: Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot, Southern_Blight, Rhizopus_Soft_Rots, Gray_Mold, Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers.

The white cottony mycelium strongly points to **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot** ("white cotton-like mycelium") or **Southern_Blight** ("white fungal mats"). Let me view a Sclerotinia reference.

The reference shows Sclerotinia at an advanced stage (bleached, hardened stem with dark sclerotia embedded). The test image shows an earlier/active stage with abundant white fluffy cottony mycelium spreading from a stem segment — this is the characteristic mycelial growth of Sclerotinia before the stem bleaches and hardens.

Key matches:
- White cotton-like mycelium (exactly matches "white cotton-like mycelium" in Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot description)
- Stem tissue affected
- The dense fluffy white growth is distinct from Rhizopus (would have black sporangia) and Southern Blight (spherical mustard-seed sclerotia on soil surface)
